reviews.review:
This is a decent sequel to the series. If you enjoyed DL1 and DL2, you’ll likely find some fun here as well.

Art – 8/10
The art is easily the strongest aspect. While it can feel a bit artificial at times, I really enjoyed the medieval fantasy aesthetic. It gives this entry a fresh style compared to previous games.

Progression – 5/10
Progression still struggles, especially in the midgame. After the first couple of cities, the experience becomes repetitive, with randomly generated layouts and little to differentiate later areas. Unique buildings, characters, or story beats tied to mid-to-late progression would add much-needed variety.

Mechanics – 5/10
Most systems remain shallow. Outside of identification and repair, other features feel optional or meaningless: quests are unrewarding, the stock market is just random numbers, the arena feels clunky, and the auction house is nearly unchanged. There’s little strategy involved, which makes them forgettable.

Suggestions for the Devs

Add simple percentage buttons (-10%, -25%, +10%, +25%) and custom input options for better control.

Make secondary mechanics more engaging: e.g., player choices influencing the stock market, bribery or tricks in the auction house, or quests with actual rewards.

Introduce unique mid-to-endgame content to keep things fresh beyond just bigger numbers.
